feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Evidence: iteration 7 (mass 0.6, y = 0.08) scored 75.92 and is the best design so far, with oval progress 0.2725, s-bend 0.1573 with oscillation 0.135, and slalom 0.1094 with 1.0 line loss per run. Iteration 8 (mass 0.5, y = 0.08) scored 55.18 because oval progress fell back to 0.12, while s-bend (0.1644) and slalom (1.0 line loss) held. So the oval gain is sensitive to mass near 0.6 kg and does not follow a monotonic trend. This iteration restores the iteration 7 geometry exactly, with the controller unchanged, so the race tests reproducibility. Plan for the next race: (1) If oval progress returns to about 0.27 and the score is near 76, the design is stable, and the team can spend the next iteration on one narrow test. Try wheel_track 0.11 at mass 0.6 and y = 0.08, since iteration 4 showed that a narrower track raises turn authority, though it also raised s-bend oscillation at y = 0.07. (2) If the oval falls back toward 0.12 again, treat the iteration 7 result as seed-sensitive and keep this geometry as the final candidate rather than moving mass further. (3) If the slalom line loss rises above 1.0 with oval progress intact, that is a controller problem, and I will address it in the controller rather than asking for more geometry change.
requested_changes: If the next race reproduces oval progress near 0.2725 with a score near 76, keep mass 0.6 and y = 0.08, and test wheel_track 0.11 as the single next change. Evidence: iteration 4 (wheel_track 0.10) lifted the score to 56.50 at y = 0.07, and oval progress only stayed flat there because the lead was limiting it, not the track.

If the next race does not reproduce the oval result (oval progress well below 0.2725), keep this geometry and do not change mass again. Evidence: iteration 8 showed that moving mass from 0.6 to 0.5 at y = 0.08 dropped oval progress from 0.2725 to 0.12, so further mass moves are not a safe lever near this point.

Do not move the forward lead beyond y = 0.08 in the next iteration. Evidence: y = 0.08 is the contract maximum, and it gave the best oval progress (0.2725) at a small cost to s-bend progress (0.1573 versus 0.1625 at y = 0.07).
